loop.top3_series_pattern: stationary, moderate seasonal, noisy, no trend, unstable model ranking
loop.top3_why: The series shows unstable model ranking and several correlated errors, so a robust, low‑variance combination is preferable. The mean of the full pool delivers the most stable per‑window performance (all ≈0.73) and avoids the high‑variance weight estimation that can occur with only three validation windows. Although its composite score is higher than the weighted alternative, the stability and robustness of the mean make it the safer choice for generalisation.
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B, while having the best composite score, relies on inverse‑error weights estimated from a very small validation set, which is prone to high variance and may overfit to the specific windows. Candidate A uses a DTW barycenter over the full pool; its per‑window performance is more erratic (especially the first window) and its score is worse than the mean. Both alternatives therefore carry higher risk of poor generalisation compared to the simple, robust mean combination.
